title.title: A cheap lane model for bowling: can a 6 MB network replace SAM 2?
title.sub: 2026-09-12 experiment loop, Tom's Gym bowling analysis
lines: The lifting side runs a small pose network per frame (MediaPipe): named landmarks in ~10 ms.
The bowling side finds the lane with SAM 2: needs a ball track first for prompts, 0.8 s per frame on CPU (tiny),
and has no lane whenever the bowler stands on it.
Question: can a YOLO11n student (2.8 M params, 6 MB) learn the lane from the three annotated videos
and give a lane on every frame, with no prompt, at 30-40 ms?

data.title: Data: three annotated videos, two unlabeled ones
data.sub: all five were shot at the same alley - generalisation here means a new camera placement, not a new venue
lines: sample_input  1080x1920 handheld, hand-clicked lane corners on every frame (180 frames)
Chardie       720x1280 handheld, static corners warped through a per-frame camera model (171 frames)
tom_old       688x1264 tripod, closest camera, lane 1.7x wider in the image than the others (409 frames)
bowling_video 1080x1920 static, wide, six lanes visible, one clean throw (417 frames, no annotation)
IMG_0242      720x1280 handheld, panning, from the seats (929 frames, no annotation)
Only these exist: the production bucket's other bowling uploads are 31 KB synthetic test clips.

method.title: Method
method.sub: same metric as the two SAM 2 loops: board MAE of the annotated ball path through the fitted lane vs the annotated lane, per frame
lines: Labels: the lane quad on EVERY frame, including frames where the bowler covers it (an amodal lane).
Students: yolo11n-seg (mask -> row extremes -> RANSAC edge lines -> corners) and yolo11n-pose (4 corner keypoints).
Training: 30 epochs on Apple MPS, heavy scale / perspective / colour augmentation, ~15-25 min per fold.
Leave-one-video-out: train on two videos, score every frame of the third. best.pt is picked on the training videos only.
Post-processing: sanity gate (RANSAC inliers >= 70 %, top width > 0 and < bottom width), carry the nearest accepted lane.
Hybrid: 3 points on the student's centre line become SAM 2 tiny's prompts - no ball track needed.
Teacher: SAM 2 tiny prompted from the engine's ball detector labels bowling_video for a '+plus' training set.
Lane selection: among the student's candidates, the mask holding the most ball-path points (SAM's component rule).

latency.title: Cost per frame on this Mac's CPU (4 threads)
lines: student seg 640     ~30 ms   6.0 MB   2.8 M params   every frame, no prompt
student seg 1024    ~58 ms   6.0 MB                  fixes the far-end width on tom_old
student pose 640    ~41 ms   5.6 MB   2.7 M params
SAM 2 tiny 1024     ~840 ms  78 MB    39 M params    needs 3 prompt points
SAM 2 base 1024     ~2100 ms 162 MB                  (loops 1-2)
student + SAM on 3 clean frames  ~3 s per throw   vs   SAM video mode  ~2 min per throw

conclusion.title: What the results say
conclusion.sub: leave-one-video-out on three videos, teacher-checked on a fourth; all at the same alley
lines: 1. Yes: a 6 MB YOLO11n-seg student learns the lane from two videos and gives one on EVERY frame,
including the frames where the bowler stands on it (Chardie 0.9 boards median, 0.65 occluded; sample_input 1.2).
2. Its weakness is WHICH lane, not precision: with several lanes in view the top box flips to the neighbour.
One anchor per video (ball path or the foul-line centre-jump rule) fixes it; SAM needs prompts on every frame.
3. The 4-keypoint pose head fails (6-11 boards): it regresses the training lanes' geometry instead of reading pixels.
4. tom_old (closest, lowest camera) is 3.1 boards at 640 px because the mask swallows a gutter's width;
at 1024 px it is 0.9 boards (100 % within 2) but the model fires on only 60 of 409 frames: width fixed, confidence not.
5. SAM 2 teacher frames from a matching placement lift sample_input 1.8 -> 1.2 boards (66 % -> 98 % within 2).
6. Student centre line -> SAM 2 tiny prompts scores 0.5-1.1 pre-hit with no ball track, on 2-3 frames per throw.
7. Trained on the teacher frames, the student copies SAM 2 to 0.13 boards on bowling_video (a training-set number).
Recommendation: ship the student as the tracker and lane picker (30-58 ms/frame, no prompt), keep SAM for the
far-end calibration on a few clean frames; grow the geometry with pseudo-labels, do not ship the pose head.
